Home.title: Authgear — Secure Login & Identity, Fully Managed
Home.description: Authgear makes it easier for developers to meet complex authentication requirements, delivering a frictionless and exceptional digital experience.
Home.heroParagraph: Open-source auth and user management for consumer and frontline identity. Start free with Passkeys, WhatsApp and SMS OTP, SAML SSO and RBAC. Run it on our cloud, in your VPC, or on your own hardware.
Home.growthSubheading: Most CIAM vendors charge extra for SSO, hold your user data hostage, and re-price you at renewal. Here is what we do instead.
Home.growthCard1Desc: Every plan, including Free, ships with passkeys, adaptive MFA, SAML SSO, Active Directory login, and RBAC. Only a custom SMS gateway and advanced security cost more. You never buy a tier to unlock a login method.
Home.growthCard2Title: Runs where your data has to live
Home.growthCard2Desc: One open-source platform, on Authgear Cloud, in your VPC, or on your own hardware. Regulated workloads stay in-region, on infrastructure you control.
Home.growthCard3Title: An exit you can actually take
Home.growthCard3Desc: Export every user, password hashes included, whenever you want. Authgear is open source and OIDC-compliant, so leaving is a decision, not a rebuild. We would rather you stay because it works.
Home.growthCard4Title: A vendor that will still be here
Home.growthCard4Desc: Bootstrapped and profitable, not raising toward an exit. Built by Skymakers, which has served enterprises worldwide for over ten years. No acquisition notice, no sunset date, no forced migration.
Home.ciamHeading:
Secure every user journey with

Authgear's tailored solutions
Home.ciamSubheading: Authgear delivers robust IAM solutions designed to meet the specific needs of your business.
Home.ciamCard1Desc: Consumers who abandon at friction. Passkeys and social login instead of passwords, WhatsApp or SMS OTP where email doesn't reach, and single sign-on across your apps so one customer stays one profile everywhere they appear.
Home.ciamCard2Desc: Frontline and deskless staff, contractors and partners. Phone-number login for people with no corporate email, batch user creation and groups for shift turnover, and ADFS or Google Workspace for office staff.
Home.ciamCard3Desc: Business customers who bring their own identity provider. SAML SSO and Microsoft Entra ID on every plan, plus roles and groups so each tenant administers its own users.
Home.microservicesHeading:
One identity across

every app you run
Home.microservicesSubheading: One sign-in for a dozen microservices or a whole product portfolio. Every service trusts the same token.
Home.microCard1Desc: Connect OIDC once and every app you operate trusts the same identity provider: web, mobile, internal tools, partner portals. The next app is a config change, not another auth integration.
Home.microCard2Desc: One identity per person across mobile, web, and partner portals. Profiles, roles and entitlements update once and apply everywhere. Every login lands in one audit log.
Home.microCard3Title: Move between apps, stay signed in
Home.microCard3Desc: App-to-app and app-to-web SSO hand an authenticated session from your mobile app straight into your web portal or your next app. No second login and no drop-off at the handoff.
Home.zeroTrustSubheading: Authgear aligns with zero-trust principles by enforcing "never trust, always verify" for every request.
Home.zeroTrustCard1Desc: Sender-constraining with OAuth DPoP binds every refresh token to a key on the device that requested it. Lift the token off that device and it won't work.
Home.zeroTrustCard2Desc: Re-authenticate users for sensitive actions: require a fresh passkey, TOTP or OTP before a transfer, permission change or account deletion.
Home.zeroTrustCard3Desc: Bot protection puts CAPTCHA on signup, login and password reset via reCAPTCHA or Turnstile. Fraud detection watches OTP patterns by IP and country, observing or blocking live.

Security shouldn't slow you down.

Ship a production login this week.

Home.buildFasterCard2Desc:
Passkeys, biometrics, and WhatsApp OTP.SMS OTP, magic links, and social login too.

BiometricAuthentication.heroTitle: Biometric Authentication Made Easy: Boost Security, Enhance User Experience
BiometricAuthentication.heroDescription: Discover how Authgear simplifies biometric authentication. Learn about the benefits, methods, and how it compares to traditional passwords. Implement effortless biometric logins today!
BiometricAuthentication.whatIsDesc: Biometric authentication is a security process that verifies a user's identity based on their unique physical or behavioral characteristics. Instead of relying on traditional methods like passwords or PINs, biometrics leverages distinctive traits such as fingerprints, facial features, or voice patterns to confirm a person's identity.
BiometricAuthentication.card1Desc: Biometric data is highly unique to each individual, making it significantly harder to compromise compared to passwords which can be easily forgotten, stolen, or guessed.
BiometricAuthentication.card2Desc: Biometric authentication offers a seamless and user-friendly experience, eliminating the need for users to remember complex passwords or carry physical tokens.
BiometricAuthentication.card3Desc: Biometric authentication adds an extra layer of protection against unauthorized access, reducing the risk of fraudulent activities.
BiometricAuthentication.card4Desc: Biometric systems can quickly and accurately verify a user's identity, providing efficient access to services and applications.
BiometricAuthentication.methodsDesc: Biometric authentication leverages various unique physical or behavioral characteristics for user verification. Let's focus on two of the most common and convenient methods: fingerprint authentication and facial recognition.
BiometricAuthentication.fp_desc: Fingerprint authentication identifies individuals based on the unique patterns and minutiae present on their fingertips.
BiometricAuthentication.fp_card1Desc: Fingerprints offer a high level of precision in identifying individuals.
BiometricAuthentication.fp_card2Desc: Fingerprint sensors are integrated into many modern devices, making them easily accessible.
BiometricAuthentication.fp_card3Desc: Fingerprint scans can be processed rapidly, providing seamless user experiences.
BiometricAuthentication.fa_desc: Facial authentication technology analyzes distinctive facial features to verify a person's identity.
BiometricAuthentication.fa_card1Desc: Facial recognition is often perceived as more convenient than other biometric methods.
BiometricAuthentication.fa_card2Desc: In some cases, facial recognition can be performed discreetly without requiring user interaction.
BiometricAuthentication.fa_card3Desc: Advanced systems can detect spoofing attempts by ensuring a live person is present.
BiometricAuthentication.flowDesc: How does biometric authentication work? Below are the key steps in biometric authentication flow:
BiometricAuthentication.flow1Desc: Upon registering biometric login, a pair of cryptographic keys is created by Secure Enclave, so the private key is protected by hardware and never left the device.
BiometricAuthentication.flow1Item1: The private key is securely stored on the user's device (Secure Enclave for iOS, Hardware-backed Keystore for Android).
BiometricAuthentication.flow1Item2: The public key is stored on the Authgear server.
BiometricAuthentication.flow2Item1: The user presents their biometric (fingerprint or face) to unlock the device's private key.
BiometricAuthentication.flow2Item2: The server sends a challenge to the devices.
BiometricAuthentication.flow2Item3: The device uses the private key to sign the challenge.
BiometricAuthentication.flow2Item4: The signed challenge is sent to the Authgear server as a response.
BiometricAuthentication.flow3Item1: The Authgear server verifies the digital signature using the stored public key.
BiometricAuthentication.flow3Item2: If the signature is valid, the user is authenticated.
BiometricAuthentication.compareTitle: Password vs. Biometric Authentication: A Comparison of Advantages and Disadvantages

BiometricAuthentication.compareSecurityPassword: Vulnerable to hacking, phishing, and brute-force attacks

SmsPumpingFraud.heroDescription: Safeguard your SMS authentication channels from costly fraud with Authgear's advanced SMS Pumping Detection. Our intelligent system identifies suspicious patterns and stops attacks before they drain your budget.
SmsPumpingFraud.threatTitle: The Hidden Threat of SMS Pumping Fraud
SmsPumpingFraud.threatDescription: SMS pumping fraud is a sophisticated attack where bad actors exploit SMS-based authentication systems by generating excessive message traffic using fake or automated phone numbers. This artificial traffic inflation can cost businesses millions in fraudulent charges while degrading legitimate user experiences.
SmsPumpingFraud.caseStudyTitle: The Twitter Case Study: A $60 Million Lesson
SmsPumpingFraud.caseStudyDescription: In late 2022, Elon Musk revealed that Twitter was losing approximately $60 million annually due to SMS pumping fraud. The fraud was traced to 390 telecom operators that allowed bot accounts to exploit Twitter's two-factor authentication system, generating fake SMS traffic to inflate their own revenue. This costly revelation highlights how even tech giants can fall victim to this growing threat.
SmsPumpingFraud.financialDrainDesc: SMS pumping attacks can rapidly deplete your messaging budget with fraudulent traffic. Companies hit by these atacks often pay between tens of thousands to millions of dollars each month in fake charges. SmsPumpingFraud.warning3Desc: One telltale sign of SMS pumping is receiving OTP requests from phone numbers with sequential patterns (e.g., numbers ending in 1000, 1001, 1002). The chance of multiple people with nearly identical phone numbers requesting OTPs simultaneously is virtually zero.
SmsPumpingFraud.warning4Desc: A noticeable drop in OTP conversion rates can indicate that fraudsters are sending requests without completing the authentication process. If your typical conversion rate falls by 20% or more, SMS pumping could be the culprit.
SmsPumpingFraud.warning5Desc: If you're burning through your SMS budget faster than usual, it's likely that SMS pumping is affecting your business. This is often the most painful symptom that finally triggers investigation.

KeycloakAlternative.faq1Q: Is there a lighter alternative to Keycloak?
KeycloakAlternative.faq1A: Authgear covers the same core standards, OIDC, SAML and MFA, with login UI, passkeys and OTP built in. You can self-host it or use our cloud, so there is less to build and maintain.
KeycloakAlternative.faq2Q: Is Authgear free and open source like Keycloak?
KeycloakAlternative.faq2A: Yes. Authgear is open source under Apache-2.0, the same licence as Keycloak, and free to self-host. You pay only for your infrastructure, and for Enterprise support if you want it. Authgear Cloud also has a free plan.
KeycloakAlternative.faq3Q: Is there a managed version of Keycloak?
KeycloakAlternative.faq3A: Not from the Keycloak project itself. Red Hat sells a supported build that you run yourself, and several third parties host Keycloak. With Authgear, the team that builds the product can run it for you, on Authgear Cloud or a private cloud.
KeycloakAlternative.faq4A: Yes. Keycloak 26 supports passkeys and WebAuthn in its standard login forms. Authgear supports passkeys too, and adds magic links, SMS and WhatsApp OTP and biometric login in mobile apps without extensions.
KeycloakAlternative.faq5Q: Can I migrate from Keycloak to Authgear?
KeycloakAlternative.faq5A: Yes. Both use OIDC and SAML, so your apps mostly need new client settings. You can import your Keycloak users with their passwords.
KeycloakAlternative.faq6Q: Where is my data stored with Authgear?
KeycloakAlternative.faq6A: Your choice. Self-host anywhere, including the UK and the EU. Authgear Cloud runs in the US or Hong Kong, and an EU region is coming soon. A private cloud we run for you can be in a UK or EU region today.

DataSovereignty.faq2Q: What's the difference between data residency and data sovereignty?
DataSovereignty.faq2A: Data residency is where the data is stored. Data sovereignty also asks who runs the system and whose law applies to that company. A US company's data centre in Europe gives you residency, not sovereignty.
DataSovereignty.faq3Q: Does the US CLOUD Act apply to my users' data?
DataSovereignty.faq3APre: It depends on who holds the data. If you self-host Authgear on a UK- or EU-owned provider, or run a private cloud on one, no US company holds your users' data.
DataSovereignty.faq3ALink: Read more about the CLOUD Act
